title: LoRA & QLoRA Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
summary: Implement Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) and 4-bit Quantized LoRA (QLoRA) using Hugging Face PEFT and bitsandbytes.
objectives: Explain the mathematical foundation of low-rank matrix decomposition: W + B*A.
Tune LoRA rank (r), alpha scaling factor, and target module matrices (q_proj, v_proj, all-linear).
Deploy QLoRA with 4-bit NormalFloat (NF4) quantization and double quantization to fit on consumer GPUs.

sections.title: The Mathematics of Low-Rank Decomposition
paragraphs: Full fine-tuning updates all billions of model weights, requiring massive VRAM for optimizer states and gradients. LoRA freezes original base weights W and injects trainable rank decomposition matrices A and B.
QLoRA quantizes the base model to 4-bit NF4 while computing gradients through 16-bit LoRA adapter matrices, enabling fine-tuning a 70B parameter model on a single 48GB GPU.

code.label: PEFT LoraConfig Setup in Python
code.code:
from peft import LoraConfig, get_peft_model, TaskType

lora_config = LoraConfig(
    r=16,
    lora_alpha=32,
    target_modules=["q_proj", "k_proj", "v_proj", "o_proj", "gate_proj", "up_proj", "down_proj"],
    lora_dropout=0.05,
    bias="none",
    task_type=TaskType.CAUSAL_LM
)

questions.prompt: What primary VRAM reduction does QLoRA achieve over standard LoRA?
choices: It quantizes the frozen base model weights into 4-bit NormalFloat (NF4).
It deletes all transformer attention layers.
It forces the model to run in 8-bit CPU memory only.
questions.explanation: QLoRA quantizes frozen base weights to 4-bit NF4 while maintaining full precision in the small trainable adapter parameters.
